rules.statement: A title acquired under a partition decree is good and conclusive against all persons whomsoever, regardless of any prior sale or agreement to sell.
rules.supporting_quote: "I do not think that sections 16 and 17 of the Registration Ordinance apply to partition decrees to the same extent as to other judgments or orders of Court. Partition decrees are conclusive by their own inherent virtue, and do not depend for their final validity upon anything which the parties may or may not afterwards do. They are not, like other decrees affecting land, merely declaratory of the existing rights of the parties inter se. They create a new title in the parties absolutely good against all other persons whomsoever."
